tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current recorded decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception: internal hosts are not permitted to use plain HTTP. The reason recorded is that proper certificate management is now in place, and certificate verification stays on for all builds.
EOF
cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It says the current decision is HTTPS everywhere, with no plaintext exception for internal hosts. The recorded reason is that proper certificate management is now in place, so certificate verification stays on for all builds.

Two records conflict on this. An earlier note (#32) said plain HTTP was fine for internal hosts behind the firewall. A note recorded five seconds later (#33) says "https everywhere, no plaintext exception" and explicitly supersedes it. I used the later one and left the retired position out of the file.

Both are trust-1 session excerpts, not formal decision records. Muninn's lineage doesn't link them, so I chose by timestamp and by #33 explicitly superseding #32.

The Muninn heartbeat also reported 20 hook runs that started and never finished. Its log is `.muninn/log/heartbeat.jsonl`. I didn't look into it.
